Halide perovskite thin-film solar cells have emerged as high-efficiency photovoltaic materials over the past decade.
The perovskite layer harvests photons through bandgap absorption across the visible spectrum, as confirmed by the external quantum efficiency spectrum.
The bandgap of the MAPbI3 perovskite is approximately 1.55 eV, well matched to the solar spectral irradiance peak.
Electron-hole pairs generated by photon absorption are subsequently separated at the perovskite-transport layer interface.
Charge extraction efficiency was quantified by transient photocurrent spectroscopy.
